answer: Latent Coordination Clustering. Each agent's transaction graph is embedded; accounts that repeatedly co-occur across a rare grove of counterparties and shared timing get linked retroactively. Enforcement: linked clusters lose accumulated reputation and future payouts, applied after review. An attacker must sustain many disjoint histories long enough to avoid correlation, paying real compute and settlement costs per identity until the river of shared edges exposes them. Detection widens as the horizon of history grows.
